messages:
sam: thinking about a 'shadow' control plane that runs a very small auth proxy in customer VPCs — caches tokens, handles local certs, and can serve token introspection to reduce roundtrips and survive central cp blips. thoughts? :thinking:
priya: interesting. main risk is secrets/keys — who holds the signing key? HSM in customer VPC? we can't ship private keys
ton y: proposal: use short-lived local signing keys provisioned by central cp via an ephemeral KDF. flow:
```
# central -> local
POST /provision-key: {customer_id, nonce}
# returns wrapped_key encrypted to customer KMS
# runtime: local signs ephemeral token, central validates signature via key ID
```
We'd rotate frequently, no long-lived key on central side.
sam: ok, but networking: do we need VPC peering/privatelink for control messages, or can local proxy call central over public egress? prefer privatelink for SLA but ops cost higher
julie: favours privatelink for enterprise customers. For self-serve tenants, allow egress-with-fallback: try privatelink, if not available use TLS over public with mTLS auth.
priya: also auditability: local proxies must stream audit logs back. can we use batched, encrypted log uploads to S3 via pre-signed URLs? infra-bot can enforce retention
infra-bot: note: audit-log stream requirement added to infra backlog #3124. retention/compliance flags required for Private customers.
tony: fallback semantics: local proxy should prefer cached tokens and local model routing. if cache miss => synchronous call to central cp with soft timeout (200ms) then degrade to token-exchange offline flow.
sam: rollout idea: start with read-only token introspection only (no sig authority) so we can test latencies and fail-open. then enable signing in a canary subset.
julie: operational playbook: circuit-breaker to disable local proxy if it falls behind, automatic key revocation path via central revoke API.
priya: security checklist: KMS integration, short key TTL, attestation (TPM), signed image verification for the proxy.
sam: ok let's capture this in an RFC follow-up. I'll sketch an interface: /v1/local/provision, /v1/local/sign, /v1/local/audit-upload. ping @eng-sre for constraints.
tony: lgtm. I'll add the sequence diagram and key lifecycle notes.
julie: +1, add metrics: cache hit rate, sign latency, fallback rate. those drive cost math.
sam: thanks all :thumbsup:
